judge_context:
Executive Summary
Open-shell organic radicals are usually unstable in air because of unsatisfied valency, but aromatic nitric acid radicals (ANARs) are stabilized by rich resonance structures that delocalize the unpaired electron over a conjugated backbone. This work reports a series of star-shaped ANARs prepared by demethylation and air oxidation of phenolic hydroxyl precursors. The materials show high spin concentration and strongly enhanced nonradiative decay, which favors photothermal conversion. The best performer, TPA-TPA-O6, reaches a solar-to-vapor efficiency of 89.41% and a water evaporation rate of 1.293 kg m⁻² h⁻¹ under 1 sun, with negligible photobleaching and excellent stability, including seawater desalination. The study positions stable organic small-molecule radicals as a low-cost, reproducible, and heavy-metal-free alternative to inorganic and polymeric photothermal materials.

Research Context
Open-shell radicals are usually unstable in air due to unsatisfied valency. Radicals are attractive for optoelectronics, magnets, photothermal, thermoelectric, and spintronics. Narrow optical band gaps can be tuned by chemical modification and structural control. Radical materials have good biocompatibility for photothermal and biological use. Organic small molecules are overlooked but avoid heavy-metal toxicity. Stable neutral radicals are rarely reported and hard to prepare. Airstable conjugated radicals are challenging due to high oxygen reactivity. Photothermal materials convert NIR light into heat via nonradiative decay.

Research Question And Hypothesis
Can stable, heavy-metal-free organic small-molecule radicals serve as efficient photothermal materials? Do star-shaped aromatic nitric acid radicals combine stability with high photothermal performance? Will high spin concentration drive nonradiative decay and boost photothermal conversion? Will TPA-TPA-O6 outperform the other three cores in photothermal and stability? Will the radical platform enable efficient solar-driven water evaporation and desalination?

Methodological Details
Four star-shaped ANARs were synthesized with different cores. Materials were made by demethylation and air oxidation of phenolic precursors. Precursors were methoxy-substituted phenol derivatives. Synthesis used only two steps with high yield and easy purification. Structures were characterized in supporting information figures. UV-vis-NIR spectra were recorded in DMSO solution and film. Cyclic voltammetry used 0.1 M nBu4NPF6 in dichloromethane. CV scan rate was 0.1 V/s. Radicals were coated on carbon-glass electrodes to form films. Potentials were referenced to SCE with Fc+/Fc internal standard. HOMO/LUMO levels were derived from CV curves. ESR was used to measure spin concentration at 0.02 mmol.

Procedures And Architectures
Demethylation and oxidation generated the neutral radicals. PLQYs were measured in dichloromethane solution and film. HOMO levels of the four radicals were measured. Photothermal tests used an 808 nm laser at 0.8 W cm⁻². Temperature was monitored with an IR thermal camera. The interfacial evaporator used white PU porous foam. TPA-TPA-O6 was loaded by impregnation and drying at 80 °C. The foam had a 2.0 cm diameter with 30 mg loading. Evaporation was tested under 1 sun (1.0 kW m⁻²). Seawater desalination reduced four primary ions.

Key Results
TPA-TPA-O6 film showed a large red-shifted radical absorption. TPA-TPA-O6 powder was black, indicating wide visible absorption. TPA-PY-O8 and TPA-TPZ-O6 showed absorption edges near 1000 nm and 800 nm. All precursors fluoresced between 450 and 570 nm. Radicals had PLQY below 1%, confirming radical formation. TPA-TPA-O6 HOMO was -4.90 eV. TPA-TPA-O6 HOMO was enhanced versus its precursor. TPA-TPA-O6 and Spiro-O8 had enhanced ESR signal intensity. TPA-TPA-O6 PLQY was 0.1%. TPA-TPA-O6 PLQY was the most quenched in the solid state. TPA-TPA-O6 powder absorption spanned 300 to 2000 nm. TPA-TPA-O6 rose from 25 °C to ~210 °C in 60 s at 0.8 W cm⁻².

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
High spin concentration drives nonradiative decay and photothermal conversion. Restricted radiative decay favors photothermal performance. Strong donor-acceptor conjugation reduces bandgap and increases paramagnetism. TPA-TPA-O6 is the best due to wide NIR absorption and high paramagnetism. The design enables future organic electronic and spintronic applications.

Contradictions And Limitations
TPA-TPZ-O6 and TPA-PY-O8 showed poor photothermal performance.

Claims
Stable open-shell aromatic nitric acid radicals are efficient, stable, and low-cost photothermal materials. TPA-TPA-O6 reached 89.41% solar-to-vapor efficiency. TPA-TPA-O6 reached 1.293 kg m⁻² h⁻¹ evaporation rate. TPA-TPA-O6 showed negligible photobleaching. TPA-TPA-O6 was stable for ten laser cycles. TPA-TPA-O6 is a pure organic small molecule. TPA-TPZ-O6 and TPA-PY-O8 had low photothermal performance. TPA-TPA-O6 may be partially protonated. The platform enables solar-driven water evaporation and desalination. The platform enables future organic electronic and spintronic applications.

TPA-TPA-O6 had the most quenched fluorescence. TPA-TPZ-O6 and TPA-PY-O8 had higher PLQY. TPA-TPA-O6 may be partially protonated. The design concept allows structural optimization. The design enables future organic electronic and spintronic applications.

Data And Code Availability
Supporting Information is available free of charge at the ACS link.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
TPA-TPA-O6 was stable for ten laser cycles. TPA-TPA-O6 temperature rose regularly with laser power. TPA-TPA-O6 recovered to ambient temperature after laser off. TPA-TPA-O6 was stable in powder and PU-dispersed states. TPA-TPA-O6 was stable in seawater desalination. TPA-TPA-O6 was cheap and easy to synthesize. TPA-TPA-O6 was soluble in green solvents. TPA-TPA-O6 had high reproducibility and solution processibility. TPA-TPA-O6 had competitive performance among organic materials. TPA-TPA-O6 had a simple synthesis with high yield. TPA-TPA-O6 had comparable performance with previous pure organic materials. TPA-TPA-O6 had a wide absorption spectrum.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is stable open-shell aromatic nitric acid radicals as efficient photothermal materials. 2. The strongest evidence is 89.41% solar-to-vapor efficiency and 1.293 kg m⁻² h⁻¹ evaporation rate. 3. The future path is developing planar ANARs for photothermal, organic electronics, spintronics, and magnetic devices.
